summary: Leonard Swidler (1929–2026) worked in religious studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from St. Norbert College, Marquette University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Tübingen. He was Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).

Leonard van der Kuijp (born 1952) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as assistant professor at the University of Washington (~1987–1995) and became professor at Harvard University in 1995.

Leopold Pospisil (1923–2021) earned degrees from Charles University, Willamette University, the University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale University from 1956 and curator of anthropology at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (~1956–1993).

Leopold von Schroeder (1851–1920) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tartu under Leo Meyer and at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu, University of Innsbruck, and University of Vienna.

Leslie S. Kawamura (1935–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Günther and served as a professor at the University of Calgary (~1976–2010).

Levi McLaughlin works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Susumu Shimazono and earned his PhD at Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. He was appointed associate professor at North Carolina State University in 2012.

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS University of London, completing an MA under Ulrich Pagel and a PhD. He held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and the University of Bonn (attested 2021).

Lewis Hodous (1872–1949) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Case Western Reserve University, Hartford International University, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served at Foochow Union Theological School (1902–1917) and Hartford International University (1917–1945).

Lewis Lancaster (born 1932) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson and Edward Conze. He held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1967–1998) and University of the West (1992).

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs (born 1942) works in Tibetology. He was president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and became Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center in 2000.
Liang Cai works in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held an attested post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas in 2014.

Libbie Mills works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 2011 and was attested teaching Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto in 2020.
Lili Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).
Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel and Swami Lakshman Joo, and held a post at the CNRS from ~1948 to 1978.
Lin He (1902–1992) was a philosopher who studied at Tsinghua University (~1919–1926) and later held a post at National Tsing Hua University.
Lin Heng is a scholar of Indology who studied at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi, earning an MA (attested 2015).
Linda Jean LaMacchia specializes in religious studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).
Linda Learman works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She was a doctoral student of Robert P. Weller and had postdoctoral mentorship under Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).
Linda Penkower specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 1993 and served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
